## `palmerpenguins` dataset

Size measurements, clutch observations, and blood isotope ratios for adult foraging Adélie, Chinstrap, and Gentoo penguins observed on islands in the Palmer Archipelago near Palmer Station, Antarctica. Data were collected and made available by Dr. Kristen Gorman and the Palmer Station Long Term Ecological Research (LTER) Program.

```{r}
#load data 
library(palmerpenguins) 
data(penguins)         
```

# Penguin Data Story

I love to play around with data and find little stories, which is what I will be asking you to do more and more as we move through the course material. So I had a little fun with the `palmerpenguins` data and this is what I came up with.

Now let's look at the `penguins_raw` version of the data. There are a bunch more variables and below is an example of what you will be able to do by the end of next week.

```{r}
penguins_raw |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_point(aes(x=`Delta 13 C (o/oo)`, y=`Delta 15 N (o/oo)`, color=Species)) +
  theme_minimal()
```

This first plot shows the 15N isotopic ratio on the y-axis plotted against the 13C isotopic ratio on the x-axis. This first plot shows the points colored by species.

::: callout-tip
## What do you see?

What is plotted? (axes, units, scale, type of plot)

How is information encoded? (color, size, shape)

What patterns are visually undeniable (trends, clusters, gradients, discontinuities)?

What do you think this figure shows?
:::

```{r}
penguins_raw |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_point(aes(x=`Delta 13 C (o/oo)`, y=`Delta 15 N (o/oo)`, color=`Body Mass (g)`)) +
  theme_minimal()
```

This second plot has the same x and y axes as the first plot, but now the points are colored by body mass.

What do you see? *(refer to the tip box above)*

If we then look at the distribution of body mass for each species in a boxplot:

```{r}
penguins_raw |>
  ggplot(aes(y=Species, x=`Body Mass (g)`)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_jitter(aes(color=Sex)) +
  theme_minimal()
```

What do you see? *(refer to the tip box above)*

What questions do these figures raise for you? What would you want to look at next?
